The controversial $3 billion corporate tax initiative Measure 97 went down in defeat, according to partial election returns Tuesday night.
Measure 97 was failing 58 percent to 42 percent as of 9:50 p.m.
The defeat follows a hard-f

ought campaign between supporters and opponents of the measure, which would have raised Washington’s minimum wage to $13.50 per hour in 2016 and $15 per hour in 2017. The initiative also would have created a new state business tax, which would have raised more than $3 billion over the next decade.
Supporters of the measure said it would have created more than 100,000 jobs and boost business with more spending by low-income people. Opponents said wages would increase too rapidly for small businesses and that the new state tax would have impacted a range of local taxes.
The measure fell short of the two-thirds majority needed for passage. The final tally will be announced Wednesday morning.
